summary: The TCP authority ledger's rule that ONLY the bootstrap node (lowest live heartbeat slot) may claim an UNOWNED page assumes bootstrap tenure is exclusive. It is not: (1) a node ranks its own slot first regardless of its own health, so a lowest-slot node whose heartbeat stalled (falsely dead, still running) keeps believing it is bootstrap; (2) every other node drops that slot from 'live' at DEATH DETECTION, before the SCSI-PR fence has landed, so the next-lowest node becomes bootstrap at once. In that window both nodes can pass activate(bootstrap)'s read-then-write on the same UNOWNED page — write + readback is not a compare-and-write: A writes seq1/ACTIVE(A), A reads back its own image, B writes seq1/ACTIVE(B), B reads back its own image; both now cache the page as MINE and both may decide grants on every resource of that page until A is fenced. Two authorities for one page = the double-grant/corruption class the ledger exists to prevent. The 0.35.4 D-0345 route (non-bootstrap masters now actively ASK the bootstrap node to claim) widens the exposure from 'pages the bootstrap decides itself' to 'every never-decided page requested during the window'.
mechanism: PROVEN sess426 (instrumented 2b, usermode): tests/tauth/bootstrap_race_test (2 vnodes, divergent views A:{A,B} B:{B}, force_bootstrap_all, A's activate held 200 ms between platter read and write via the new ledger knob activate_hold_once_ms): before the fix A rc=0 EX AND B rc=0 EX on the same resource; A mine=1 B mine=1; platter ACTIVE(A) seq=5 after B's ACTIVATE seq=2 + grant seq=3 — A's write (base = the UNOWNED image at seq 1) became the highest seq and ERASED B's activation and committed grant. Root (dlm/tauth_store.c mxfs_tauth_page_write, pre-0.36.0): the write re-read only the copies' seqs (next=max+1, target=spare copy) and verified only its own copy's readback; nothing tied the commit to the image the caller patched. The bootstrap election cannot be made exclusive at the requester (a falsely-dead node cannot know), so the ledger write itself must arbitrate. || DESIGN-PROVEN interleaving (instrument step 1/2 pending): A = slot 1 (HB thread stalled > death timeout, process alive), B = slot 2. B: node_track[1].live=false -> lowest_live_slot()==2 -> bootstrap_cb true. A: lowest_live_slot()==1 (own slot short-circuit). Page P UNOWNED. A: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED, write ACTIVE(A) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. B: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED (before A's write lands) , write ACTIVE(B) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. Platter ends ACTIVE(B); A's cache says ACTIVE(A). A's later txn commits are page writes that overwrite B's (same-seq race is only -EIO if the readback happens to see the other image). Fence of A lands seconds later. Also needs proof of whether the death->fence ordering (fence_before_recovery) covers the bootstrap election: if the election waited for fence completion (mxfs_disklock node_track fenced flag) the window closes for (2) but not for (1) (A never learns it is dead until its own writes fail).
